1.note: כִּידוֹד is the rare word of Job 41:11 כִּידוֹדֵי אֵשׁ, "sparks of fire". Here: the longing for home burned in him.

2.note: The sea is drawn as a thief: it denies the thing in its keeping (the language of Lev 5:21), but at times "the theft is found in his hand" (Exod 22:3), when the ship comes up again. "Tongue of the sea" (Isa 11:15) is a bay or arm of the sea; here it is also the tongue that denies.

3.note: בֵּית מַרְזֵחַ is a house of mourning in Jer 16:5, but מַרְזֵחַ is a revelling feast in Amos 6:7. The wailing passengers fit the first sense; the second may also be heard in the noise and loss of control.

4.note: The rhyme words of lines 2 and 3 differ only by one vav: עֹנִי "poverty" and עוֹנִי "one who answers me". The play cannot be kept in English.
